title: The Tiger Gets the House Keys
skyStory: The moon storms into Aries at first quarter, half lit, half shadow, all attitude. This is Joel's sign, and the moon has arrived like a guest who kicks the door open and shouts greetings at everyone. Mars, ruler of Aries, has made a welcome banner in red marker. It is crooked. Nobody cares. The cabin chimney is pumping smoke like a locomotive.

reading: Aries moon, first quarter, and the whole sky is at your back. You will feel unstoppable before lunch. Use it. Pick the scariest item on your list, the one that has been glaring at you, and pounce. The [[Knight of Wands]] has been waiting all month for this exact morning.

One note from the moon, delivered with love: do not start four new things just because you can. First quarter moons are about decisions. Decide one. Then, around 7 pm, tell somebody the story of how you did it, and add one wildly exaggerated detail. Life Path 3 rules allow exactly one.
joel.mission: Pounce on the scariest item on your list before noon, then roar quietly at your desk to celebrate.
joel.omen: A red car parked perfectly straight. It means today, your aim is true.

reading: The moon has gone off to stay with Joel for a couple of days, and it has turned his volume knob all the way up. You will feel it from miles away: a burst of messages, an idea in all caps, a plan with seventeen steps. Your job today is the oldest job in your friendship. Be the mountain.

Saturn, your ruler, and Mars, his, are shaking hands today instead of arguing. That is rare. Use it. Ask him the one question that turns seventeen steps into three. The [[Queen of Pentacles]] is right there in your pocket, practical and warm. Then go do something just for you.
nancy.mission: Turn somebody's big messy plan into three clear steps today, then take a victory sip of something warm.
nancy.omen: A ram, a goat or a sheep anywhere, even on a sign. It means Aries and Capricorn are in agreement today.
nancy.stoneWhy: a steady mountain for a fiery day

together.text: Joel shares the scariest thing he pounced on. Nancy shares the smartest question she asked. Then you swap roles for one sentence: Joel asks a careful question, Nancy pounces on an idea. Mars and Saturn will both be confused, which is very good for them.
